- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Oktoberfest: One of the most famous beer festivals in the world, held annually from late September to early October.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tollwood Winter Festival: Held in December and January, featuring a diverse range of events including performances, markets, and cultural events.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Frühlingsfest: Held in late April and early May, similar to Oktoberfest but with a spring theme.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Munich Film Festival: Held annually in June/July, showcasing international cinema with screenings, premieres, and interactive events.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Christkindlmarkt: Held during Advent, featuring Christmas markets, food, music, and cultural events.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Auer Dult: Held three times a year, featuring a variety of fairs including a May fair, summer fair, and fall fair.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Streetlife Festival: Held in May and September, taking place over an entire weekend with street performances, music, and food.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Munich Opera Festival: Held in July, featuring performances by renowned opera companies from around the world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Starkbierfest: Celebrates strong beer, often dubbed the "little sister of Oktoberfest," taking place in March.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Long Night of Music: Held in June, with Munich's music venues staying open late into the night for live performances across the city.
